claims.text: A pre-formed Cr-rich or multicomponent passive film is the governing structural mediator of corrosion resistance in high-performance alloy steels used in chemical-processing and nuclear-power applications.
The as-fabricated microstructure, particularly grain-boundary density, promotes optimal formation of the passive film.
The passive film enables rapid self-healing and limits corrosion under combined chemical, thermal, and irradiation stresses.
As-fabricated steels normally possess native passive films, fabrication-related surface oxidation, and a characteristic grain-boundary density.
Controlled thermal or chemical pre-oxidation can modify passive-film thickness and composition.
Annealing or pre-oxidation can modify grain-boundary exposure.
Passive-film thickness, Cr-rich composition, and uniformity govern the ability of the steel to repassivate rapidly.
Optimized pre-treatment enhances formation of a dense, self-healing passive oxide layer.
A compact, self-healing oxide layer acts as a diffusion barrier against corrosive species and further oxidation.
Increased grain-boundary density accelerates oxide regeneration.
Rapid oxide regeneration mitigates corrosion during simultaneous thermal and irradiation stresses.
Pre-treated steels with enhanced passive films will have significantly lower corrosion rates and corrosion currents than untreated as-fabricated steels under identical conditions.
Pre-treated steels with enhanced passive films will develop a more uniform oxide scale than untreated as-fabricated steels.
The mechanism should hold in corrosive chemical-processing and nuclear-power environments involving temperature fluctuations and moderate radiation exposure.
The mechanism may not apply in ambient or non-corrosive settings.
The magnitude of corrosion-rate reduction depends on passive-film kinetics, alloy composition, and environmental stressors.
A lack of statistically significant corrosion improvement, or a lack of correlation between corrosion resistance and film or grain-boundary changes, would falsify the proposed governing mechanism.
